status: Source-backed discovery hypotheses and cost mechanisms; not recommendations or return evidence.

mechanisms.name: Collateralized inventory replacement while a bridge is in flight
mechanisms.classification: Historical author-reported execution; current economics unverified
mechanisms.economic_cause: Inventory on the receiving chain permits the sale leg before delayed bridged inventory arrives.
mechanisms.who_pays: Price-taking flow producing the market gap; the borrower pays financing, collateral and execution costs.
mechanisms.why_might_recur: Non-atomic settlement and fragmented inventories recur, but speed/capital competition can consume the gap.
mechanisms.asset_equivalence: Borrowed debt asset must be exactly deliverable by the bridge output, with matching contract, issuer and units. Ticker matching is insufficient.
mechanisms.contract_evidence: Six exact paper-linked transaction references in findings.md; no explorer receipt or current reserve/contract verification.
mechanisms.inventory_lifecycle: Preposition eligible collateral; borrow the receiving-chain asset; sell; receive bridged replacement; repay principal plus accrued debt; release collateral.
mechanisms.capital_access: Ordinary collateralized borrowing, not a free flash loan. Borrow caps, eligible collateral, LTV/liquidation rules and <=2x delta-neutral feasibility unverified.
costs_risks: Both execution legs, failed attempts and infrastructure
mechanisms.cheapest_falsifier: At the exact proposed asset/reserve, borrowed output cannot be repaid by the bridge claim, no borrow headroom exists, or executable gap is below financing plus all-in cycle costs.
mechanisms.qualification: No actual current T2/T3, independent risk approval or probability gate.

mechanisms.name: Value repayment-chain choice as an inventory service
mechanisms.classification: Documented cost optimization, not standalone arbitrage
mechanisms.economic_cause: Across LP-fee and relayer economics depend on where replenished inventory is needed and where repayment is requested.
mechanisms.who_pays: Bridge user pays the quoted fee; LP and relayer components compensate different services.
mechanisms.why_might_recur: Directional customer flow continually changes chain balances. Existing relayers already implement inventory management, so the feature is not a novel uncaptured edge.
mechanisms.asset_equivalence: Exact source/destination assets, bridge route and repayment token must match; fee components must use consistent units.
mechanisms.contract_evidence: Official fee and running-relayer docs only; no selected deployed contract, quote, fill or repayment receipt.
mechanisms.inventory_lifecycle: Fill from destination inventory, wait for bundle reimbursement, receive repayment, then restore target balances by real opposing flow or a separately costed rebalance.
mechanisms.capital_access: Prefunded inventory and competitive fill eligibility are required; nomination/access and attainable fill share unverified.
costs_risks: Zero origin-repayment LP fee is not zero total fee
mechanisms.cheapest_falsifier: Whole-cycle replenishment cost and capital delay exceed the LP-fee saving or user fee; no accessible profitable fill remains.
mechanisms.qualification: No new relayer installed or activated; no deployment recommendation.

mechanisms.name: Legitimate bridge-pool rebalancing surplus with an independent return rail
mechanisms.classification: Explicit documented payer; no executable current cycle
mechanisms.economic_cause: Some cBridge xLiquidity StableSwap pairs can pay more destination tokens for flow restoring pool balance.
mechanisms.who_pays: LP inventory value/impermanent loss funds the output improvement; it is not free issuance or a negative all-in fee.
mechanisms.why_might_recur: External one-way demand can recreate imbalances, but rebalancing consumes the finite state-dependent surplus.
mechanisms.asset_equivalence: Exact issuer/bridge claims and pool pair must be established. An unrelated native-USDC CCTP rail cannot automatically return any USDC.e or other variant.
chains_protocols: Independent return rail only if exact assets are supported
mechanisms.contract_evidence: Registry available but extracted section labels were ambiguous; no contract selected as a verified xLiquidity pool or route.
mechanisms.inventory_lifecycle: Provide beneficial rebalancing flow; close the cycle through genuine opposing flow or an independently supported and costed route; restore initial inventory.
mechanisms.capital_access: Sufficient pool inventory and exact route eligibility unverified.
costs_risks: Base/protocol fee may exceed price deviation
mechanisms.cheapest_falsifier: A full-size current quote after all fees has no positive cycle margin, or the supposed cheap return rail does not accept the actual destination token.
mechanisms.qualification: Documentation example is not an observed fill or evidence of repeated profit.

mechanisms.name: Unified prefunded EURC inventory across EVM and Solana
mechanisms.economic_cause: An issuer-native unified balance can reduce duplicated chain inventory and allow response to actual same-claim price differences.
mechanisms.who_pays: Any genuine trading surplus comes from executable market price differences; Gateway does not itself promise yield.
mechanisms.why_might_recur: Chain-specific demand can fragment liquidity, but this public rail may also compress the basis for all competitors.
mechanisms.asset_equivalence: EURC on each exact supported chain/mint, not EURC versus USDC and not cirBTC versus WBTC. Separate balances per asset do not perform FX or BTC-claim conversion.
chains_protocols: Other announced chains are research context, not a proposed allocation
mechanisms.contract_evidence: Issuer 2026-10-23 launch and Solana operational pre-mint announcement. Actual tradable EURC mints, Gateway contracts and on-chain deployment state not independently verified.
mechanisms.inventory_lifecycle: Deposit and finalize prefunded escrow; use authorized minting on the needed chain; close market legs and restore the unified balance. This is not uncollateralized borrowing or cross-chain atomic execution.
mechanisms.capital_access: Prefunding, signature authority, service availability and applicable eligibility/terms must be verified. No account or signer used.
costs_risks: Seven-day fallback withdrawal described by issuer
mechanisms.cheapest_falsifier: Exact EURC contracts/route eligibility do not match, no accessible executable same-claim gap exists, or full-cycle fees/capital cost erase any inventory saving.
mechanisms.qualification: Pre-mint stock is not circulating liquidity and the operational account must never receive user deposits. No approved allocation or risk-tier upgrade.

mechanisms.name: New cross-VM asset distribution as a basis watchlist
mechanisms.classification: Recent deployment lead only, not demonstrated arbitrage
mechanisms.economic_cause: Newly connected representations may face fragmented liquidity; native redemption/transport cost determines whether an apparent price difference is a tradeable basis.
mechanisms.who_pays: Market flow, if an executable same-claim spread exists; no bridge-issued free profit is assumed.
mechanisms.why_might_recur: Adoption and liquidity can be uneven; public transport also tends to compress the gap.
mechanisms.asset_equivalence: Exact ITS token_id, Solana mint, origin asset and redeemability must agree. Symbol equality is insufficient.
chains_protocols: Stellar/SHx and Hedera/SAUCE as issuer-reported launch examples
mechanisms.contract_evidence: 2026-06-03 official mainnet-live announcement plus transfer guide; no exact live token mint/program, pool or receipt verified.
mechanisms.inventory_lifecycle: Establish matched redeemable claims, prefund or lawfully finance sale inventory, transport and restore inventory; concrete cycle not selected.
mechanisms.capital_access: Token liquidity, exact program configuration, route limits and access unknown.
mechanisms.cheapest_falsifier: No matching redeemable token mapping or no independently executable pool depth on both sides.
mechanisms.qualification: Watchlist, not a selected strategy; do not infer profits from a launch announcement.

mechanisms.name: Stablecoin variant convergence through an actual redemption path
mechanisms.classification: Added candidate pressure test; contract identities verified from docs, full cycle not established
mechanisms.economic_cause: An immediate market sale can discount a bridge-backed claim relative to native issuer tokens because redemption consumes time, capital and risk.
mechanisms.who_pays: The seller demanding immediate liquidity; the converter bears actual bridge, issuer, capital, execution and operating costs.
mechanisms.why_might_recur: Recurring imbalanced flow could recreate a basis, but liquidity migration, competition or fee/term changes can remove it.
mechanisms.asset_equivalence: See conversion-matrix.json: exact Ethereum native USDC, Arbitrum native USDC and Arbitrum USDC.e are distinct contracts with distinct rails and rights.
mechanisms.contract_evidence: Three asset addresses and native CCTP rail registry documented. Current USDC gateway mapping/backing, AMM pool and live route capacity not verified.
mechanisms.inventory_lifecycle: Hypothetically buy exact USDC.e with native Arbitrum USDC, redeem to Ethereum native USDC, then CCTP back to Arbitrum native USDC. Not a direct CCTP variant conversion.
mechanisms.capital_access: Conditional bridge redemption rather than assumed retail issuer fiat access; present gateway terms, caps, minimums and user's legal eligibility remain unknown.
costs_risks: Withdrawal dispute interval and capital lock
mechanisms.cheapest_falsifier: Any exact-contract redemption leg is unsupported or no executable discount exceeds all measured cycle costs and capital lock.
mechanisms.qualification: No complete current executable conversion path, repeatable net basis, T2/T3 or independent risk approval. USDT/USDT0 and USDG intentionally unresearched.
